mechanism: S(T+1) - S(T) = log p+(T) - log p-(T), so a marker distribution saturated toward '+' makes the clean candidate win by margin rather than by content. Every log p+ term is <= 0, so S(T+1) accumulates a near-zero penalty while every error candidate pays log p-(j).
conclusion: If implied p+ is near 1 and the predicted-clean rate far exceeds the actual clean rate, the deficit is in the MARKER SURFACE FORM (which this project declares as its own — the paper publishes no prompt or code), not in the Eq. 6 arithmetic. Report it as a property of our reconstruction of their baseline. Do NOT retune the prompt against ProcessBench labels.
not_a_fix: Changing the marker tokens, system message, or decision rule to raise F1 on these rows would be tuning on evaluation labels. Any such change must be pre-registered and evaluated on rows held out from this diagnosis.
